evidence.source: wiktionary
evidence.text:
Ideogram (指事) - three parallel strokes. Compare with 一, one stroke meaning “one”, 二, two strokes meaning “two”, and 亖, four strokes meaning “four”.
Triplication of 一 (“one”). See also 畺. Unrelated to 丰.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *kV-sum.
Pronunciation in Early Middle Chinese should be *srim, but actually is *sam, with a non-retroflex initial consonant. This irregular development should be due by analogy with the initial of number four in EMC, *sijH.

evidence.field: 字形演變; 商代、金文、篆書 image records
evidence.text: The page identifies 三 as U+4E09 and lists a Western Zhou bronze inscription record (集成04261), followed by Chu manuscripts and the Shuowen seal form. It explains the three equal horizontal strokes as three counting rods representing the number three. The page's early-form images are not textually described beyond the Western Zhou bronze record.
evidence.title: 漢字「三」：字形演變

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.field: 數詞﹛三﹜的用字演變研究（一）, §2.1.1 商朝數詞{三}的用字
evidence.text: The article reports numeral 三 in Shang oracle-bone corpus examples H.16189 and H.37453, and says its corpus survey found a single graph slot, 三, used for the numeral in the Shang period. This supports a Late Shang attestation of the numeral use; it does not supply a precise year for either inscription.
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.text: The survey reports that Zhou-period sources added 參 as another way to write the numeral, while 三 remained dominant; it gives an example from a Western Zhou late-period bronze inscription and reports another numeral-writing form 品/晶 in Warring States manuscript material. It reports 三 and 參 in Qin-Han excavated texts. These are orthographic alternatives for the numeral, not evidence that the basic graph 三 was borrowed from another word.
evidence.kind: scholarly article reporting historical orthographic uses
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research, Wu Yuanyuan
evidence.text: The article notes one transmitted Hanshu example using 叄 for numeral 三 but excludes it from the Qin-Han count, reasoning that it may reflect later character substitution; its survey found no such form for the numeral in excavated Qin-Han documents. This is a proposed textual-transmission caveat, not proof that the form was impossible in the period.
evidence.kind: scholarly article; author’s qualified textual assessment
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說明; 說文釋形; 形體資料表
evidence.text: The dictionary gives the Shuowen account: 三 means the way of Heaven, Earth, and humanity, and is formed from the numeral three; it records the ancient form 弎 as 三 written with 弋. Its entry also indexes a Shuowen seal form and lists ancient-script reference works, but several oracle-bone and bronze resources are marked unavailable. Xu Shen's cosmic gloss is a historical lexicographic interpretation; the counting-rod analysis is a separate modern paleographic explanation.
evidence.title: [A00004] 三 - 教育部《異體字字典》 臺灣學術網路十四版（正式七版）2024

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi with Duan Yucai commentary

evidence.text: The entry transcribes 許慎: 「天地人之道也。从三數。凡三之屬皆从三。」 It also records 「古文三从弋」 for 弎. Duan Yucai distinguishes the definition from graphic explanation and comments that the graph's three strokes embody the three powers. This confirms the transmitted account but is not an independent Shang-period attestation.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
